name: Germany

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: García-Condado et al. 2019 (GCB Bioenergy): EU28 total 419 Mt × Germany ~14% share; cross-checked against Wietschel et al. 2013 (Applied Energy): Germany average 60.8 Tg/yr gross × ~30% recoverable
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Gross crop residue production ~60 Mt odt/yr; recoverable fraction ~40% (cereal straw) leaving 24 Mt. Major crops: winter wheat, barley, rye, rapeseed, maize stover.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: Thrän et al. 2016 (Bioresource Technology): Germany technical biomass potential from wood industry and forestry; Eurostat roundwood 72 Mm³/yr 2023; logging residue factor ~0.14 odt per m³
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Germany is largest roundwood producer in EU. High existing utilization (~75%) constrains additional residues. Includes logging residues and processing residues from sawmills and pulp mills.

msw_total_mt.notes: Near 50 Mt total; Germany has among highest MSW rates in EU at 606 kg/capita.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: SCHEMA.md EU default; Eurostat waste composition data; EU biogenic fraction ~0.50
msw_biogenic_frac.notes: Food + garden waste dominant biogenic fractions; paper partially biogenic.

msw_treatment.source: Eurostat env_wasmun 2022; CEWEP 2022 municipal waste treatment report; Germany leads EU in recycling/composting at 69% (some sources show ~64% recycle+compost, ~35% WtE)

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: Holm-Nielsen et al. 2009; JRC biogas potential dataset (jrc-10076-10002); Germany accounts for ~53% of EU biogas production, livestock density data. EU 1.4 Gt wet manure/yr; Germany share ~13% × dry matter fraction ~10%
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Germany has >9000 biogas plants, most in EU. Cattle + pig slurry dominant. Dry-matter basis ~10-12% of wet weight.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: Eurostat/EEA sewage sludge data; EU total ~9-10 Mt dry matter/yr; Germany share ~10% of EU population with high treatment coverage
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: Germany generates ~800-900 kt dry sewage sludge/yr. Increasing incineration due to phosphorus recovery regulations.

nutrient_status_source: FAO fertilizer use data; Germany has some intensive livestock zones (Bavaria, Lower Saxony) with localized excess, but overall national status is moderate; Nitrates Directive compliance improving
notes: Germany has Europe's largest biogas sector. Significant existing AD infrastructure. Forestry residues already highly utilized. Priority residues: cereal straw, rapeseed, manure for existing biogas.

name: France

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: García-Condado et al. 2019 (GCB Bioenergy): France 84 Mt/yr gross crop residues, ~30% recoverable = 33.6 Mt; JRC Brief JRC109294
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: France is #1 EU crop residue producer. 84 Mt gross, 40% recoverable = ~34 Mt odt. Cereals 70-75% of residues (wheat dominant). Oilseeds (rapeseed, sunflower) also significant.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: Eurostat forestry statistics; France roundwood production ~48 Mm³/yr 2023; logging residue factor ~0.12-0.15 odt/m³; Gasparatos & Stromberg 2019 spatial forest biomass assessment
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: France has substantial forest cover (~31% of land area) but lower harvest intensity than Nordic countries. Processing residues from sawmills significant.

msw_total_mt.notes: ~36.6 Mt total MSW 2022.

msw_treatment.source: CEWEP 2022; Eurostat env_wasmun 2022

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: JRC biogas manure dataset; EU total manure 1.4 Gt wet; France ~8-9% share of EU livestock; dry matter conversion
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: France has large cattle sector (dairy + beef). Wet manure ~120 Mt/yr × ~10% DM = ~12 Mt odt.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: EEA/Eurostat sludge data; EU ~9-10 Mt dry/yr; France ~9% share
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: High WWTP coverage. ~850 kt dry matter/yr.

nutrient_status_source: FAO fertilizer use; Nitrates Directive implementation; Brittany region has localized excess from intensive pig/poultry but national average moderate
notes: Largest EU crop residue base. Brittany has excess nutrients (pig density). Good candidate for BECCS if storage available (Jurassic/Paris Basin). Forestry sector large but residues already utilized for heat.

name: Italy

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: García-Condado et al. 2019: Italy in top 7 EU residue producers; JRC 2018 brief. Italy ~8-9% of EU28 419 Mt total = ~34-38 Mt gross × 30% = ~14 Mt recoverable
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Maize stover dominant in Po Valley (Pianura Padana). Wheat straw in center/south. Olive/vine prunings significant (~2-3 Mt additional). Prunings excluded from main estimate but noted.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: Biomass resources and costs EU countries (Ericsson & Werner 2011 Biomass Bioenergy); Italy harvesting costs highest in EU (74 €/Mg) limiting technical availability
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Italy has large forest area but steep terrain limits mechanized harvesting. Low mobilization rate. Processing residues from wood industry moderate.

msw_total_mt.notes: ~29 Mt total 2022.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: EU average; Italian waste composition data; high organic fraction due to Mediterranean diet
msw_biogenic_frac.notes: Slightly above EU average biogenic fraction.

msw_treatment.source: CEWEP 2022; Eurostat env_wasmun 2022; Italy has high recycling rate

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: JRC biogas manure dataset; FAO livestock Italy; Po Valley intensive pig/cattle sector
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Po Valley has intensive pig (suino) and dairy cattle. Wet manure ~90 Mt × 10% DM. Padania region has localized excess nutrients.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: EEA sludge data; Italy ~7% of EU population, good WWTP coverage in north
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: Southern Italy has lower WWTP coverage reducing total.

nutrient_status_source: Po Valley has localized excess (nitrates derogation areas); national average moderate; south Mediterranean-type low-input farming
notes: Po Valley is highest-density ag residue zone in Italy. Significant olive/vine pruning residues not captured in main estimate. Strong WtE sector in north.

name: Spain

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: García-Condado et al. 2019: Spain top 7 EU producer; JRC brief. Spain ~9-10% of EU28 total = ~38-42 Mt gross × 30% = ~15-17 Mt recoverable. Nature/Sci Reports 2026: bioenergy potential of straw residues from southern Spain
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Diverse: cereal straw (central meseta), sunflower/rapeseed, olive prunings (Andalucía), vine prunings. Olive prunings ~4-5 Mt additional but moisture/collection challenges.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: S2BIOM project; Ericsson & Werner 2011; Spain has large forested area but moderate harvest intensity and high wildfire risk reducing sustainable residue removal
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Eucalyptus plantations in Galicia/Asturias contribute pulpwood residues. Moderate logging residue potential limited by steep/remote terrain.

msw_total_mt.notes: ~22.7 Mt total 2022.

msw_treatment.source: CEWEP 2022; Eurostat 2022; Spain relatively low WtE, higher landfill share vs NW Europe

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: JRC biogas manure dataset; Spain has large pig sector (2nd largest EU pork producer); 31% slurry lagoon use (EEA/Eurostat livestock)
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Catalonia and Aragon have intensive pig production with excess nutrients. Large dairy cattle sector also significant.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: EEA sludge data; Spain ~6% EU population

nutrient_status_source: Catalonia/Aragon pig zones = localized excess; Meseta generally low-input; national average moderate
notes: Diffuse landscape, high transport costs for residue collection. Olive prunings and vine cuttings are distributed point sources. WtE penetration low — landfill dominant. Potential for bio-oil/biochar for diffuse residues.

name: Poland

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: García-Condado et al. 2019: Poland 3rd/4th largest EU28 residue producer; JRC 2018 brief. Poland ~10-11% of EU28 419 Mt = ~42-46 Mt gross × 30% = ~17-18 Mt recoverable
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Cereals dominant: winter wheat, rye (Poland is main EU rye producer), triticale, barley. Rapeseed significant. Gross ~45 Mt odt/yr × 40% = 18 Mt recoverable.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: Eurostat forestry statistics; Poland significant roundwood producer; S2BIOM; forest cover ~31% of land area
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Large state-managed forests (Lasy Państwowe). Significant pine/spruce logging residues. Processing residues from wood industry also substantial.

msw_total_mt.notes: Lower per-capita generation than EU average.

msw_treatment.source: CEWEP 2022; Eurostat 2022; Poland expanding WtE capacity

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: JRC biogas manure dataset; Poland ~7.5% EU manure N (dairy cattle dominant, EEA livestock 2020); FAO livestock Poland
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Large dairy cattle and pig sector. Growing biogas sector. Wet manure ~100 Mt × 10% DM.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: EEA sludge data; Poland ~5% EU population; WWTP coverage improving but below NW Europe average
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: ~500 kt dry matter/yr. Increasing with EU UWWTD compliance.

nutrient_status_source: FAO fertilizer data; Poland has moderate fertilizer intensity; Nitrates Directive compliance improving; no systematic excess comparable to NL/DK
notes: Large contiguous arable plains enable concentrated collection. Poland #1 EU rye producer. Growing biogas sector. Coal-heavy energy system creates political tension for biomass pathways.

name: Romania

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: García-Condado et al. 2019: Romania 4th largest EU producer due to maize dominance; JRC brief. Romania ~8-9% of EU28 total = ~34-38 Mt gross × 30% = ~14 Mt recoverable
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Maize stover dominant (Romania largest EU maize producer). Wheat straw also significant. High variability due to drought years. Danube Plain concentration.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: Eurostat forestry statistics; Romania significant forest cover ~30%; FAO FRA 2020; significant illegal logging limits sustainable residue estimates
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Carpathian forests are significant. Legal harvest ~20 Mm³/yr but actual higher. Processing residues from wood industry notable.

msw_total_mt.notes: Lowest per-capita MSW generation in EU. Official figures likely undercount informal sector.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: World Bank What a Waste 2.0; Romania has higher organic fraction in waste stream consistent with lower-income country profile
msw_biogenic_frac.notes: Higher biogenic fraction due to larger food waste share.

msw_treatment.source: CEWEP 2022; Eurostat 2022; Romania has very high landfill rate, facing EU infringement

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: FAO livestock Romania; JRC manure dataset; large cattle + pig sector, some subsistence farming
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Romania has large but fragmented livestock sector. Many small farms complicate manure collection. Wet manure ~70 Mt × 10% DM.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: EEA wastewater data; Romania has lowest WWTP connection rate in EU (~60%); Eurostat urban wastewater
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: Low WWTP coverage severely limits sludge volumes. Only ~150 kt dry matter/yr.

nutrient_status_source: FAO fertilizer use per ha; Romania has below-EU-average fertilizer intensity; nutrient depletion in some soils is a concern
notes: High landfill rate creates opportunity for WtE+CCS upgrade. Maize stover is dominant feedstock — excellent BECCS candidate if storage identified. Low WWTP coverage is a major infrastructure gap.

name: Netherlands

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: S2BIOM project; Eurostat crop production Netherlands; small arable area (1.8 Mha) dominated by vegetables/potatoes/sugar beet; JRC brief
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Limited cereal area. Potato haulm, sugar beet tops, and vegetable residues are main streams. High-value horticultural residues often composted/AD.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: Eurostat forestry statistics; Netherlands has minimal commercial forest (360 kha); mostly small-scale parks/windbreaks
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Negligible logging residues. Mainly wood processing waste imported. Urban wood waste more significant.

msw_total_mt.notes: ~8.1 Mt total 2022.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: EU average; Dutch waste composition data

msw_treatment.source: CEWEP 2022; Eurostat 2022; Netherlands has very high WtE rate, near-zero landfill

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: JRC biogas manure dataset; Netherlands has highest livestock density in EU per ha; ~40% slurry lagoon use (EEA); Nitrates Directive chronic derogation
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Extreme livestock density: 100M+ chickens, 12M pigs, 4M cattle in 3.5 Mha. Total wet manure ~80 Mt × 10% DM = 8 Mt odt. Massive phosphate/nitrogen surplus.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: EEA sludge data; Netherlands ~2.2% EU population but near 100% WWTP coverage; primarily incinerated for P recovery
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: ~220 kt dry matter. Most sludge mono-incinerated (phosphorus recovery). Negligible agricultural application.

nutrient_status_source: FAO fertilizer data; Nitrates Directive chronic derogation expiring; highest N emissions in EU from agriculture (EEA); systematic manure surplus exceeding 170 kg N/ha limit
notes: EXCESS nutrient status — biomass burial/removal pathways strongly favored. Manure is the primary feedstock concern. High WtE rate means MSW pipeline largely committed. Vaulted-type biomass waste injection ideal. Government actively reducing livestock numbers (stikstofcrisis).

name: Belgium

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: S2BIOM project; Eurostat crop production Belgium; small arable area ~850 kha; wheat, maize, sugar beet, potatoes dominant crops
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Sugar beet leaves, wheat straw, maize stover. Small absolute volumes due to country size.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: Eurostat forestry statistics; Belgium ~23% forest cover (700 kha); Ardennes beech/oak forests
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Ardennes forest generates modest logging residues. Some processing residues from wood industry.

msw_total_mt.notes: High per-capita generation (4th in EU). ~7.9 Mt total 2022.

msw_treatment.source: CEWEP 2022; Eurostat 2022; Belgium has high recycling rate

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: JRC biogas manure dataset; FAO livestock Belgium/Flanders; Flanders has extreme livestock density similar to Netherlands; Nitrates Directive compliance issues
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Flanders (northern Belgium) has intensive pig/poultry. Wallonia more extensive cattle. Total wet manure ~45 Mt × 10% DM. Low emission application mandatory in Flanders.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: EEA sludge data; Belgium ~1.3% EU population, near full WWTP coverage

nutrient_status_source: Flanders systematic nitrogen/phosphorus surplus; Nitrates Directive chronic violations; MAP (Manure Action Plan) successive rounds; Flanders comparable to Netherlands in nutrient excess
notes: EXCESS nutrient status (Flanders). Small country but very high feedstock density for manure. WtE infrastructure well-developed. Good candidate for AD+CCS or biomass waste injection.

name: Czechia

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: S2BIOM project D5.3; Eurostat crop production Czechia; ~3.5 Mha arable land; wheat, barley, rapeseed, maize dominant crops
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Cereal straw (wheat, barley) dominant. Rapeseed straw significant. Gross ~12-13 Mt × 40% = ~5 Mt recoverable.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: Eurostat forestry statistics; Czechia ~34% forest cover; major bark beetle crisis 2018-2022 created large salvage harvest volumes; FAO FRA 2020
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Massive bark beetle (Ips typographus) outbreak drove unusually high harvest 2018-2022, generating large residue volumes. Spruce monocultures being replaced. Processing residues from wood industry significant.

msw_total_mt.source: Eurostat env_wasmun 2022; ~490 kg/capita (estimated) × 10.7M population; Czechia data not in all Eurostat tables
msw_total_mt.notes: Estimated ~5 Mt total. Some Eurostat tables show n/a for CZE 2022.

msw_treatment.source: CEWEP 2022; Eurostat 2022; Czechia expanding WtE

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: FAO livestock Czechia; JRC manure dataset; cattle and pig farming concentrated
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: ~35 Mt wet manure × 10% DM = 3.5 Mt odt.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: EEA sludge data; Czechia ~1% EU population, good WWTP coverage

nutrient_status_source: FAO fertilizer data; Czechia moderate fertilizer intensity; some intensive livestock zones but no systematic excess
notes: Bark beetle crisis 2018-2022 created unusual residue surplus now declining. Transitioning to mixed forest will reduce future spruce residue volumes. Growing WtE sector.

name: Greece

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: S2BIOM project; Eurostat crop production Greece; ~3.6 Mha arable; cotton stalks, wheat straw, olive prunings, corn stover, tobacco residues
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Cotton stalks are significant (Greece is main EU cotton producer). Olive prunings add ~1-1.5 Mt. Wheat straw in Thessaly/Macedonia. Gross ~11 Mt × 40% = ~4.5 Mt.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: Eurostat forestry statistics; Greece ~67% forested/shrubland but low commercial harvest; high wildfire risk discourages residue mobilization
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Most forest is maquis/phrygana scrubland with low commercial value. Actual logging residues limited. Wildfire risk means leaving residues increases fire hazard.

msw_total_mt.notes: ~5.6 Mt total 2022.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: EU average; Greek waste composition; high organic fraction (Mediterranean diet)

msw_treatment.source: CEWEP 2022; Eurostat 2022; Greece has near-zero WtE, very high landfill rate facing EU infringement

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: FAO livestock Greece; sheep/goat dominant (largest in EU per capita), plus cattle and pigs
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Greece has large small-ruminant sector (sheep + goats) — 9M+ head. Extensive grazing reduces manure concentration. Difficult to collect.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: EEA sludge data; Greece ~1% EU population; WWTP coverage improving but incomplete on islands

nutrient_status_source: FAO fertilizer use; Mediterranean low-intensity farming; extensive grazing; well below EU average fertilizer use per ha
notes: High landfill rate creates MSW opportunity but no WtE infrastructure. Diffuse ag residues (cotton, olives) favor bio-oil/biochar. Island geography complicates logistics. No viable geologic storage identified nearby.

name: Portugal

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: S2BIOM project; Eurostat crop production Portugal; ~1.9 Mha arable; wheat, maize, olive prunings, vine cuttings
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Olive prunings (~0.5 Mt) and vine cuttings significant alongside cereal straw. Eucalyptus plantations generate separate woody stream counted under forestry.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: Ericsson & Werner 2011 (lowest harvesting cost in EU 27 €/Mg for Portugal); S2BIOM; eucalyptus plantations dominant in central Portugal
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Eucalyptus (Eucalyptus globulus) plantations for pulp generate significant processing residues. Lowest harvesting cost in EU. Wildfire risk creates urgency for residue removal (fire fuel reduction co-benefit).

msw_total_mt.notes: ~5.2 Mt total 2022.

msw_treatment.source: CEWEP 2022; Eurostat 2022

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: FAO livestock Portugal; JRC manure dataset; moderate-intensity livestock
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Cattle (dairy + beef) and pig farming. Wet manure ~25 Mt × 10% DM.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: EEA sludge data; Portugal ~1% EU population

nutrient_status_source: FAO fertilizer data; Portugal below EU average fertilizer intensity; Mediterranean low-input farming; soils often nutrient-poor
notes: Eucalyptus processing residues and wildfire-risk forest fuels are key opportunity. BECCS via Portucel/Navigator pulp mills potentially viable. Wildfire co-benefit from residue mobilization is strong policy hook.

name: Sweden

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: Eurostat crop production Sweden; ~2.6 Mha arable; cereal straw (wheat, barley, oats, rapeseed); S2BIOM project Sweden NUTS3 data
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Limited arable land relative to forest. Cereal straw dominant. Some used as fodder/bedding — competing use reduces recoverable fraction.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: Karlsson et al. 2026 (GCB Bioenergy): Sweden total biomass surplus 5.75 Mt DM plus additional potential; Sköldberg et al. 2020 (Forest Biomass Availability Springer): unutilized 13.7 TWh/yr logging residues; Eurostat roundwood 71.8 Mm³/yr 2023
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Sweden is Europe's 2nd largest roundwood producer. Logging residues (GROT - grenar och toppar) = branches/tops. Large mill processing residues (bark, sawdust). High existing utilization for district heating. Sustainable additional potential ~9-10 Mt odt/yr.

msw_total_mt.notes: ~4 Mt total 2022. Low per-capita MSW despite high income — strong waste prevention/recycling culture.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: EU average; Swedish waste composition data

msw_treatment.source: CEWEP 2022; Avfall Sverige statistics 2022; Sweden imports waste for WtE. Near-zero landfill.

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: FAO livestock Sweden; JRC manure dataset; predominantly cattle (dairy), some pigs
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: ~25 Mt wet manure × 10% DM = 2.5 Mt odt. Extensive rather than intensive farming.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: EEA sludge data; Sweden ~1% EU population, near 100% WWTP coverage; Stockholm Exergi BECCS project context
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: ~180 kt dry matter/yr. Stockholm Exergi (KVV8) captures CO2 from biomass combustion including sludge.

nutrient_status_source: FAO fertilizer use; Sweden extensive farming, low fertilizer intensity; nutrient-poor soils in many forest areas
notes: Forestry is the dominant feedstock. Stockholm Exergi already operating BECCS (CCS on biogenic WtE). Sweden has existing BECCS infrastructure and deep geologic storage (Sleipner proximity). Leading BiCRS nation in Europe.

name: Hungary

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: García-Condado et al. 2019: Hungary in top EU maize residue producers; S2BIOM; Eurostat crop production. Hungary ~4.5 Mha arable; maize, wheat, sunflower, rapeseed. Gross ~17 Mt × 30% = ~7 Mt.
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Maize stover dominant (Hungary major EU maize producer in Danube basin). Wheat straw also significant. High variability between drought and wet years.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: Eurostat forestry statistics; Hungary ~22% forest cover; FAO FRA 2020; mainly oak and beech with some pine
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Moderate forest sector. Growing utilization for biomass energy. Processing residues from wood panel/furniture industry.

msw_total_mt.notes: ~3.9 Mt total 2022.

msw_treatment.source: CEWEP 2022; Eurostat 2022; Hungary still heavily landfill-dependent

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: FAO livestock Hungary; JRC manure dataset; cattle, pig, poultry sector
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Wet manure ~40 Mt × 10% DM = 4 Mt odt.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: EEA sludge data; Hungary ~1% EU population; WWTP coverage ~90%

nutrient_status_source: FAO fertilizer data; Hungary moderate fertilizer use; some intensive livestock areas but not systematic excess
notes: Great Plain (Alföld) provides concentrated maize and wheat residue base. High landfill rate is infrastructure gap. Danube Plain proximity to potential storage basins.

name: Austria

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: S2BIOM project; Eurostat crop production Austria; ~1.4 Mha arable; wheat, maize, barley, rapeseed dominant
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Relatively small arable area due to mountainous terrain. Cereal straw and maize stover main streams. Gross ~7 Mt × 40% = ~2.8 Mt recoverable.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: Eurostat forestry statistics; Austria ~47% forest cover; roundwood ~20 Mm³/yr; Austria is major forest country per capita; Gasparatos 2019 spatial assessment
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Austria has strong forestry sector (47% land area forested). Spruce/pine logging residues. Significant wood processing residues (sawmills, particleboard). High existing utilization for biomass district heating.

msw_total_mt.source: Eurostat env_wasmun 2022; ~803 kg/capita × 9.1M population — highest per-capita in EU
msw_total_mt.notes: ~7.4 Mt total 2022. Austria generates most MSW per capita in EU (803 kg). May reflect tourism sector waste.

msw_treatment.source: CEWEP 2022; Eurostat 2022; Austria near-zero landfill, high WtE and recycling

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: FAO livestock Austria; JRC manure dataset; cattle (dairy + beef) dominant, mountainous pastoral farming
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Extensive mountain farming with cattle. Wet manure ~25 Mt × 10% DM = 2.5 Mt odt.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: EEA sludge data; Austria ~0.9% EU population, near 100% WWTP coverage

nutrient_status_source: FAO fertilizer data; Austria moderate intensity farming; alpine grazing is low-intensity; no systematic excess
notes: Forestry is the dominant sector. Austria already a major biomass energy user. High per-capita MSW is notable — tourism influence. Near-zero landfill shows mature waste management.

name: Denmark

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: S2BIOM project; Eurostat crop production Denmark; ~2.6 Mha arable (63% of land area); cereals dominant (winter wheat, barley), rapeseed, sugar beet
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Very high arable land fraction (63% of national territory). Wheat/barley straw dominant. Sugar beet leaves significant. Gross ~9 Mt × 40% = ~3.5 Mt recoverable.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: Eurostat forestry statistics; Denmark ~14% forest cover; mostly beech and conifer plantations; low overall forest area
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Limited forest resource. Some processing residues from wood industry. Orsted co-firing uses imported biomass — domestic forestry residues minor.

msw_total_mt.source: Eurostat env_wasmun 2022; ~802 kg/capita × 5.8M population — 2nd highest in EU
msw_total_mt.notes: ~4.7 Mt total 2022. High per-capita generation (2nd in EU after Austria).

msw_treatment.source: CEWEP 2022; Eurostat 2022; Waste Incineration Nordic Countries 2024; Denmark has highest WtE share in EU

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: JRC biogas manure dataset; Denmark has intensive pig industry (~13M pigs, 2× human population); Nitrates Directive chronic compliance issues; EEA livestock data
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Extreme pig density: ~13M pigs in 5.8M population country. Total wet manure ~60 Mt × 10% DM = 6 Mt odt. Manure surplus area designation widespread.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: EEA sludge data; Denmark ~0.6% EU population, near 100% WWTP coverage

nutrient_status_source: Nitrates Directive compliance; Denmark has systematic N/P surplus from pig density; Action Programme under NVZ; one of highest livestock N loads per ha in EU
notes: EXCESS nutrient status. Highest WtE share in EU — MSW pipeline already committed (Orsted Kalundborg etc.). Manure is primary uncaptured stream. Biogas already large but scaling AD+CCS has strong economics. Excellent North Sea CO2 storage access.

name: Finland

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: S2BIOM project; Eurostat crop production Finland; ~2.2 Mha arable; barley, oats, wheat, rapeseed; cold climate limits yields
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Limited by northern climate. Cereal straw and oat/barley residues. Short growing season limits residue quality. Gross ~4-5 Mt × 35% = ~1.5 Mt recoverable.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: IEA Bioenergy Task 31/43; Asikainen et al. IEA Bioenergy 2015: Finland logging residues 2.2 Mm³/yr; consumption of forest residues 7-8 Mm³/yr 2013-2018; Eurostat roundwood 63.5 Mm³/yr 2023; conversion 0.25 odt/m³ solid wood equivalent
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Finland is Europe's 3rd largest roundwood producer. Massive forest industry (UPM, Stora Enso, Metsä Group). Logging residues (GROT) + stumps + mill by-products. High existing utilization for heat/power. Sustainable additional mobilization possible ~9 Mt odt/yr.

msw_total_mt.notes: ~2.9 Mt total 2022.

msw_treatment.source: CEWEP 2022; Eurostat 2022; Waste Incineration Nordic Countries 2024; Finland high WtE, notable landfill share remaining

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: FAO livestock Finland; cattle and pig farming; relatively low livestock density vs. NW Europe
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Wet manure ~20 Mt × 10% DM = 2 Mt odt.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: EEA sludge data; Finland ~0.5% EU population, near 100% WWTP coverage

nutrient_status_source: FAO fertilizer use; Nordic extensive farming; forest soils nutrient-poor; below EU average fertilizer intensity
notes: Forestry overwhelmingly dominant. Large pulp/paper/sawmill sector (UPM, Stora Enso, Metsä, Sappi) as retrofit BECCS candidates. High WtE share for MSW already. Baltic/North Sea storage proximity excellent.

name: Ireland

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: S2BIOM project; Eurostat crop production Ireland; ~1.0 Mha arable; barley, wheat, oats dominant. 2020 UK biomass survey used as regional proxy (6.3 Mt technical UK; Ireland ~10% proportional)
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Small arable area dominated by grassland. Cereal straw modest. Some baled straw potential. Many Irish farms are dairy/beef pastoral with minimal arable residues.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: Coillte forest service Ireland; Eurostat forestry statistics; Ireland forest cover ~11% and growing; Sitka spruce plantations
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Sitka spruce plantation forests reaching harvest maturity. Growing residue stream. Processing residues from new mills. Low current utilization — significant upside.

msw_total_mt.source: Eurostat env_wasmun 2022; n/a in some tables; estimated ~520 kg/capita × 5.1M population
msw_total_mt.notes: Eurostat shows n/a for Ireland in some 2022 tables. Estimate based on EU average per capita × population.

msw_treatment.source: CEWEP 2022; EPA Ireland waste statistics 2022

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: FAO livestock Ireland; intensive dairy cattle sector (post-milk quota expansion); JRC manure dataset
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Ireland has very high cattle density (~7M cattle in 7M ha). Predominantly dairy since milk quota abolition 2015. Wet manure ~35 Mt × 10% DM = 3.5 Mt odt. Nitrates Directive compliance challenge.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: EEA sludge data; Ireland ~0.5% EU population

nutrient_status_source: Nitrates Directive compliance; Ireland has Nitrates Action Programme; some zones exceed 170 kg N/ha from dairy intensification
notes: Dairy cattle manure is dominant wet feedstock. Growing forestry sector offers future woody stream. Diffuse agricultural landscape. Limited geologic storage identified — biomass burial possible if nutrients allow. No WtE+CCS currently.

name: Bulgaria

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: S2BIOM project; Eurostat crop production Bulgaria; ~3.5 Mha arable; wheat, sunflower, maize, barley dominant
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Significant crop area. Wheat straw and sunflower stalks dominant. High variability. Some informal burning of residues in field. Gross ~12 Mt × 40% = ~5 Mt recoverable.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: Eurostat forestry statistics; Bulgaria ~36% forest cover; FAO FRA 2020; beech and conifer forests in mountains
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Mountain forests (Balkans, Rhodopes) with moderate commercial harvest. Significant processing residues from wood industry. Growing bioenergy sector.

msw_total_mt.notes: ~3.4 Mt total 2022.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: World Bank What a Waste 2.0; Bulgaria higher organic fraction consistent with lower-income profile

msw_treatment.source: CEWEP 2022; Eurostat 2022; Bulgaria high landfill rate facing EU infringement proceedings

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: FAO livestock Bulgaria; cattle, sheep, pig, poultry sector; declining livestock post-1990
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Large sheep/goat sector traditionally. Wet manure ~30 Mt × 10% DM. Fragmented farming reduces collection efficiency.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: EEA sludge data; Bulgaria ~0.6% EU population; low WWTP coverage (~67%)
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: ~60 kt dry matter/yr. Low WWTP coverage limits sludge volumes.

nutrient_status_source: FAO fertilizer use; Bulgaria below EU average fertilizer intensity; some soil nutrient depletion from post-communist farm restructuring
notes: High landfill rate creates MSW opportunity. Field burning of residues common — collection infrastructure needed. Low fertilizer use = biomass removal favored. Limited WtE infrastructure.

name: Croatia

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: S2BIOM project; Eurostat crop production Croatia; ~1.5 Mha arable; maize, wheat, soybean, sunflower
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Slavonia region has concentrated maize/wheat production. Gross ~4-5 Mt × 40% = ~1.8 Mt recoverable.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: Eurostat forestry statistics; Croatia ~37% forest cover; Croatian Forests Ltd state enterprise; oak and beech dominant
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Croatian Forests (HŠ) manages ~80% of state forests. Moderate harvest intensity. Processing residues from wood industry in Slavonia.

msw_total_mt.notes: ~1.9 Mt total 2022.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: EU average; slightly higher organic fraction in Balkan context

msw_treatment.source: CEWEP 2022; Eurostat 2022; Croatia predominantly landfill, one WtE plant planned for Zagreb

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: FAO livestock Croatia; mixed cattle/pig/poultry sector
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Wet manure ~15 Mt × 10% DM = 1.5 Mt odt.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: EEA sludge data; Croatia ~0.4% EU population; WWTP coverage ~65%, improving
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: ~40 kt dry matter/yr. Low WWTP coverage limits sludge.

nutrient_status_source: FAO fertilizer data; Croatia below EU average fertilizer intensity; traditional mixed farming
notes: Small country, moderate residue base. Slavonia eastern region has concentrated ag residues. High landfill rate is infrastructure gap.

name: Slovakia

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: S2BIOM project; Eurostat crop production Slovakia; ~1.4 Mha arable; wheat, barley, maize, rapeseed, sugar beet
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Cereals dominant in Danube lowlands. Gross ~6 Mt × 40% = ~2.5 Mt recoverable.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: Eurostat forestry statistics; Slovakia ~41% forest cover; spruce/beech/fir; significant bark beetle impacts similar to Czechia
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Mountain forests (Tatras, Carpathians). Bark beetle crisis also affected Slovakia. Processing residues from wood/furniture industry.

msw_total_mt.notes: ~2.6 Mt total 2022.

msw_treatment.source: CEWEP 2022; Eurostat 2022

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: FAO livestock Slovakia; cattle, pig farming
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Wet manure ~20 Mt × 10% DM = 2 Mt odt.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: EEA sludge data; Slovakia ~0.5% EU population

nutrient_status_source: FAO fertilizer data; Slovakia moderate intensity farming
notes: Mixed ag/forestry resource base. Danube lowlands for ag residues; Carpathian forests for woody. Wood processing is significant industry.

name: Lithuania

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: S2BIOM project; Eurostat crop production Lithuania; ~2.9 Mha arable (45% of territory); wheat, rye, barley, rapeseed, sugar beet
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Substantial arable land relative to country size. Cereal straw dominant. Rapeseed straw significant. Gross ~6 Mt × 40% = ~2.5 Mt.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: IEA Bioenergy Nordic/Baltic assessment: Lithuania forest fuel potential ~1.4 Mm³; Bioenergy technologies Baltic ScienceDirect 2020; Eurostat forestry
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: ~33% forest cover. Pine/spruce/birch mix. Growing bioenergy use. Processing residues from wood panel/furniture industry (IKEA supply chain significant).

msw_total_mt.notes: ~1.3 Mt total 2022.

msw_treatment.source: CEWEP 2022; Eurostat 2022; Kaunas WtE plant significant

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: FAO livestock Lithuania; dairy cattle dominant; JRC manure dataset
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Wet manure ~20 Mt × 10% DM = 2 Mt odt.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: EEA sludge data; Lithuania ~0.3% EU population

nutrient_status_source: FAO fertilizer data; Lithuania moderate farming intensity; improving practices post-EU accession
notes: Balanced ag+forestry resource base. Growing bioenergy sector. Baltic Sea proximity for potential offshore storage. IKEA supply chain drives certified forest management.

name: Slovenia

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: S2BIOM project; Eurostat crop production Slovenia; ~170 kha arable; maize, wheat, hops dominant; mountainous terrain limits arable
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Very small arable area due to alpine/karst terrain. Maize stover and wheat straw modest.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: Eurostat forestry statistics; Slovenia ~58% forest cover — highest in EU after Finland; active forest management
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Highest forest cover in EU outside Nordics. Beech/fir/spruce forests. Significant processing residues. Wood industry important export sector.

msw_total_mt.notes: ~1 Mt total 2022.

msw_treatment.source: CEWEP 2022; Eurostat 2022

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: FAO livestock Slovenia; mostly cattle (dairy + beef) in alpine meadows
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Wet manure ~7 Mt × 10% DM = 0.7 Mt odt.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: EEA sludge data; Slovenia ~0.2% EU population

nutrient_status_source: FAO fertilizer data; Slovenia mixed farming, below EU average intensity; alpine grazing extensive
notes: Forestry is dominant. High forest cover creates significant but already heavily utilized woody biomass resource.

name: Latvia

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: S2BIOM project; Eurostat crop production Latvia; ~1.8 Mha arable; cereals (wheat, rye, barley, oats), rapeseed, potatoes
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Moderate arable area. Cereal straw dominant. Gross ~4 Mt × 35% = ~1.5 Mt recoverable.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: Bioenergy technologies Baltic ScienceDirect 2020: Latvia forest fuel potential ~24 TWh/yr technically available; Eurostat forestry; Latvia ~52% forest cover
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Very high forest cover (52%). Pine/spruce/birch. Forest fuels are major energy source (92.4% of renewables from biomass). High existing utilization but substantial additional potential.

msw_total_mt.notes: ~0.9 Mt total 2022.

msw_treatment.source: CEWEP 2022; Eurostat 2022; Latvia near zero WtE, predominantly landfill

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: FAO livestock Latvia; cattle (dairy) and pig farming
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Wet manure ~12 Mt × 10% DM = 1.2 Mt odt.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: EEA sludge data; Latvia ~0.2% EU population

nutrient_status_source: FAO fertilizer data; Latvia low-intensity farming; extensive land abandonment since 1990s
notes: Forest dominant. High landfill rate is major gap. Near Baltic Sea for potential offshore storage. Biomass already ~92% of renewables — strong cultural/industrial alignment.

name: Estonia

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: S2BIOM project; Eurostat crop production Estonia; ~820 kha arable; cereals (barley, wheat, rye), rapeseed, potatoes
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Small arable area. Cereal straw dominant. Gross ~2 Mt × 40% = ~0.8 Mt recoverable.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: Bioenergy technologies Baltic 2020: Estonia ~6.2 Mm³/yr available forest fuel (moderate scenario) = ~13.5 TWh/yr; primary supply biomass 12 TWh 2010; Eurostat forestry; Estonia ~52% forest cover
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Very high forest cover. Pine/spruce/birch. Growing harvest with infrastructure development. Potential 300 kha additional agricultural land for energy forestry.

msw_total_mt.notes: ~0.58 Mt total 2022.

msw_treatment.source: CEWEP 2022; Eurostat 2022

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: FAO livestock Estonia; cattle and pig farming
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Wet manure ~7 Mt × 10% DM = 0.7 Mt odt.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: EEA sludge data; Estonia ~0.15% EU population

nutrient_status_source: FAO fertilizer data; Estonia extensive farming, significant land abandonment; low input intensity
notes: Small but forest-rich country. Biomass energy well-developed. High landfill rate being addressed. Baltic Sea proximity for storage.

name: Luxembourg

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: S2BIOM project; Eurostat crop production Luxembourg; ~130 kha arable; cereals (wheat, barley), rapeseed, hay
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Very small arable area. Gross ~0.3 Mt × 40% = ~0.12 Mt. Negligible scale for BiCRS strategy.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: Eurostat forestry statistics; Luxembourg ~34% forest cover; ~87 kha forest; mostly beech and oak; Ardennes continuation
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Small absolute forest area. Processing residues from wood industry minor.

msw_total_mt.source: Eurostat env_wasmun 2022; ~721 kg/capita × 0.64M population — 3rd highest in EU
msw_total_mt.notes: ~0.45 Mt total 2022. High per-capita due to cross-border workers and transit economy.

msw_treatment.source: CEWEP 2022; Eurostat 2022; Luxembourg high recycling culture

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: FAO livestock Luxembourg; mostly dairy cattle; small country
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Wet manure ~2 Mt × 10% DM = 0.2 Mt odt.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: EEA sludge data; Luxembourg ~0.06% EU population

nutrient_status_source: FAO fertilizer data; Luxembourg moderate intensity farming; Moselle Valley viticulture
notes: Tiny biomass base. MSW is the most significant per-capita feedstock. Not a strategically significant standalone BiCRS site; aggregate with Belgium or cross-border projects.

name: Cyprus

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: S2BIOM project; Eurostat crop production Cyprus; ~130 kha arable; cereals (wheat, barley), citrus, potatoes, grapes
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Small island, limited arable. Cereal straw modest. Citrus prunings add small amount. Gross ~0.25 Mt × 40% = ~0.1 Mt.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: Eurostat forestry statistics; Cyprus ~18% forest cover but mostly protected state forest; very limited commercial harvest
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Troodos mountain forests largely protected. Commercial forestry negligible.

msw_total_mt.source: Eurostat env_wasmun 2022; ~673 kg/capita × 1.17M population — 5th highest in EU
msw_total_mt.notes: ~0.79 Mt total 2022. Elevated per-capita due to tourism sector waste.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: Mediterranean diet drives higher organic fraction; World Bank What a Waste 2.0 proxy
msw_biogenic_frac.notes: Higher biogenic fraction due to food waste in tourist economy.

msw_treatment.source: CEWEP 2022; Eurostat 2022; Cyprus heavily landfill-dependent, facing EU infringement

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: FAO livestock Cyprus; mostly sheep, goats, poultry, some cattle
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Wet manure ~1.5 Mt × 10% DM = 0.15 Mt odt.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: EEA sludge data; Cyprus ~0.1% EU population; good WWTP coverage in urban areas

nutrient_status_source: FAO fertilizer data; Mediterranean extensive farming; below EU average fertilizer use
notes: Island geography limits biomass logistics. MSW most concentrated stream. No viable geologic storage identified. High landfill rate is critical gap. Not a priority standalone BiCRS site.

name: Malta

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: Eurostat crop production Malta; ~12 kha arable — smallest arable area in EU; vegetables, potatoes, wine grapes
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Negligible. Malta has almost no commercial crop residues.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: Eurostat forestry statistics; Malta <1% forest cover; mostly urban parks
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: No commercial forestry.

msw_total_mt.notes: ~0.31 Mt total 2022. Tourism-inflated per-capita figure.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: Mediterranean profile; higher food waste fraction
msw_biogenic_frac.notes: Tourist economy inflates food waste biogenic fraction.

msw_treatment.source: CEWEP 2022; Eurostat 2022; Malta largely landfill-dependent, limited WtE

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: FAO livestock Malta; small poultry and pig sector
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Minimal livestock.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: EEA sludge data; Malta ~0.05% EU population

nutrient_status_source: Limited agriculture; not a significant nutrient-status country for BiCRS purposes
notes: Minimal biomass resources — smallest EU member state by land area. MSW is the only relevant feedstock. Island geometry rules out most pathways. Not a standalone BiCRS site.

name: United Kingdom

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: UK Dept for Energy Security/DESNZ 2020 Biomass Survey: theoretical potential 24.98 Mt DM, technical potential 6.3 Mt DM; UK Biomass Strategy 2023
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: UK 2020 agricultural departments survey gives 6.3 Mt DM technical potential. Cereal straw (wheat, barley, oats) dominant. Some oilseed rape. Scotland and East England concentrated.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: UK Biomass Survey 2020: theoretical 1.4 Mt DM, technical 0.5 Mt DM; Forestry Commission GB statistics
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Limited domestic forest compared to biomass demand. Drax and other large BECCS plants rely heavily on imported wood pellets (US SE, Baltic). Domestic residue potential modest.

msw_total_mt.source: DEFRA UK Statistics on Waste 2022: households 25.691 Mt; total municipal ~27-28 Mt including commercial fraction
msw_total_mt.notes: Household waste ~25.7 Mt 2022; ~44.1% recycled per WRAP/DEFRA.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: IPCC/Kaplan; UK waste composition surveys; slightly above EU average due to food waste fraction
msw_biogenic_frac.notes: UK biogenic fraction ~0.55 based on composition surveys.

msw_treatment.source: DEFRA/UK statistics on waste 2023-24: incineration 50.2%, landfill 5.5%, recycling 44.1% of local authority waste

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: FAO livestock UK; JRC manure dataset proxy (UK ~same scale as Ireland+NI livestock); cattle (dairy+beef), sheep, pigs
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Large cattle and sheep sector. Wet manure ~120 Mt × 10% DM = 12 Mt odt. Includes N. Ireland intensive dairy.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: EEA/ENDS Europe data; UK ~1.0 Mt dry sewage sludge/yr pre-Brexit; Eurostat EU-15 historical data shows UK similar to Germany
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: UK among top EU/EEA sludge producers alongside Germany, France, Spain. ~1.0 Mt dry/yr.

nutrient_status_source: DEFRA nutrient management data; UK has Nitrate Vulnerable Zones but national average moderate; Somerset Levels etc. localized issues
notes: Drax Power Station is Europe's largest BECCS project (imports wood pellets — not domestic residues). UK has world-leading WtE+CCS policy framework. Domestic ag residues modest relative to large population. North Sea CO2 storage (Acorn, Viking, HyNet) excellent.

name: Norway

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: S2BIOM project; Eurostat/FAO Norway crop data; ~930 kha arable; cereals (barley, oats, wheat), hay/silage dominant
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Limited arable area in harsh climate. Most farming is grass-based livestock. Cereal straw potential modest. Gross ~2 Mt × 40% = ~0.8 Mt.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: SINTEF Norway BiCRS assessment: sustainably available biomass 1-13 Mt CO2 removals potential; FAO FRA 2020 Norway roundwood ~10 Mm³/yr; Biomes/CarbonGap Norway tracker 2026
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Norway has large productive boreal forests. Spruce/pine logging residues. Processing residues from Norske Skog, Borregaard etc. High existing utilization for pellets export and domestic heat.

msw_total_mt.source: SSB Norway waste statistics; Norway generates ~450-480 kg/capita × 5.4M population; EEA Norway waste data 2022
msw_total_mt.notes: ~2.2 Mt total 2022. Norway imports waste from UK/Ireland for WtE — domestic waste insufficient for existing capacity.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: EU/EEA average proxy; Norwegian waste composition data

msw_treatment.source: SSB Norway avfallshandtering; Incineration economy Norway ScienceDirect 2024; Norway ~28% incineration in 2023 data but accounting differs

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: FAO livestock Norway; mostly cattle (dairy), sheep/goats in mountain regions
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Wet manure ~15 Mt × 10% DM = 1.5 Mt odt.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: EEA sludge data; Norway ~0.5% EU/EEA population, near 100% WWTP coverage

nutrient_status_source: FAO fertilizer data; Norway extensive farming; high cost of N fertilizer discourages overuse; marine nutrients dominate coastal areas
notes: Norway is strategically critical for BiCRS: Sleipner (1996) and Northern Lights storage, world-class offshore CO2 infrastructure. Forestry residues are the primary feedstock. Oslo WtE (Klemetsrud/Fortum) is key BECCS site. Strong government support.

name: Switzerland

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: S2BIOM proxy; Swiss Federal Office for Agriculture; ~1.1 Mha arable; cereals (wheat, barley), maize, sugar beet, potatoes
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Limited arable land (mountainous). Cereal straw and maize stover. Gross ~2 Mt × 40% = ~0.8 Mt recoverable.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (BAFU); Switzerland ~31% forest cover; ~5 Mm³/yr roundwood harvest; S2BIOM proxy
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Switzerland has sustainable forest management with high processing residues. Saw timber, pulpwood, energy wood well-developed. Wood is major energy source (district heating).

msw_total_mt.source: Swiss Federal Statistics Office; ~671 kg/capita × 8.8M population; BAFU waste statistics 2022
msw_total_mt.notes: ~6 Mt total 2022. Zero landfill (banned since 2000). ~50% recycled, ~50% incinerated.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: EU/Swiss average; Swiss waste composition studies

msw_treatment.source: BAFU Switzerland; Cleantech-Alps report; Switzerland 100% WtE+recycling, zero landfill since 2000

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: FAO livestock Switzerland; mostly cattle (dairy) in alpine pastures; pig farming in lowlands
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Wet manure ~18 Mt × 10% DM = 1.8 Mt odt.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: EEA proxy; Switzerland ~0.7% EU/EEA population; near 100% WWTP coverage

nutrient_status_source: Swiss federal agricultural data; moderate intensity farming; alpine extensive grazing; nitrogen surplus issues in some lowland cantons
notes: Zero landfill, 100% WtE+recycling — existing WtE infrastructure (KVA plants) are excellent BECCS retrofit candidates. No geologic CO2 storage within Switzerland — would need cross-border pipeline. Biomass already heavily utilized for district heating.

name: Ukraine

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: SAF Ukraine / biomass energy review; Ukraine crop residue theoretical potential >111 Mt/yr (wheat, barley, maize, sunflower); accessible dry mass wheat ~9.6 Mt (2024 baseline scenario); recoverable ~30% of theoretical = ~44 Mt. War disruption (2022-) creates high uncertainty.
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Ukraine is among world's top crop residue producers. Theoretical 111 Mt/yr × 40% = ~44 Mt recoverable. Major crops: winter wheat, sunflower stalks, maize stover, barley. War since Feb 2022 severely disrupts harvests and logistics. Wide uncertainty range reflects wartime conditions.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: FAO FRA 2020 Ukraine; S2BIOM EU neighborhood coverage; Ukraine ~16% forest cover; Carpathian and Polesia forests
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Significant forests in Carpathians and northern Polesia. War-related harvest disruption 2022-. Pre-war logging residues estimated at ~4 Mt odt/yr.

msw_total_mt.source: World Bank What a Waste 2.0 (2018): Ukraine ~14 Mt/yr pre-war; population displacement and war reduce 2022-2025 estimates significantly; calc: ~0.4 Mt/yr reduction per 1M displaced persons
msw_total_mt.notes: Pre-war ~14 Mt/yr. Population fell from ~44M to ~37M by 2023 due to war displacement. Estimated ~10-11 Mt 2022. Very high uncertainty. Predominantly landfilled.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: World Bank What a Waste 2.0; Ukraine similar to Eastern European profile with higher organic fraction
msw_biogenic_frac.notes: Higher biogenic fraction consistent with lower-income Eastern European profile.

msw_treatment.source: World Bank What a Waste 2.0 2018; Zerowaste Ukraine; predominantly landfill/dump disposal

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: FAO livestock Ukraine pre-war; Ukraine had ~3.8M cattle, 6M pigs, 200M poultry pre-2022; wartime livestock losses significant
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Pre-war ~120 Mt wet manure × 10% DM = ~12 Mt odt. War has reduced livestock numbers substantially. Wide uncertainty range.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: Proxy estimate: Ukraine ~40M population pre-war × 5 kg dry sludge/capita/yr (lower than EU due to WWTP coverage ~70%); war disruption
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: WWTP coverage partial pre-war (~70%). War infrastructure damage reduces actual output further.

nutrient_status_source: FAO fertilizer data; Ukraine had moderate fertilizer use on black soil (chernozem) belt; disruption since 2022 reduces inputs
notes: Ukraine has among largest ag residue potential in Europe (chernozem belt). All estimates highly uncertain due to ongoing war (Feb 2022-). Post-war reconstruction could enable major BiCRS development. Proximity to potential Black Sea or Dnieper-Donets basin storage. Data should be reviewed annually.

name: Serbia

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: SAF/Jefferson Institute biomass Serbia: 12.5 Mt annual biomass, 9 Mt (72%) agricultural; ~9 Mt × 55% recoverable (higher fraction for Balkan context) = ~5 Mt. Wheat, maize, sunflower, soy dominant.
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Serbia biomass study: 9 Mt/yr agricultural biomass total. Major crops in Vojvodina plain: maize, wheat, sunflower, soybean. Vojvodina is one of most productive agricultural regions in Balkans.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: Jefferson Institute Serbia biomass: ~3.5 Mt total biomass from forestry; 30-40% recoverable fraction; FAO FRA proxy
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: ~30% forest cover. Beech/oak/pine in Dinaric highlands. Processing residues from wood industry (furniture export).

msw_total_mt.source: World Bank Serbia Municipal Waste Situational Analysis 2023; Serbia 2022: 2.95 Mt municipal waste, 473 kg/capita
msw_total_mt.notes: ~2.95 Mt total 2022. Official figures; actual may be higher with informal sector.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: World Bank What a Waste 2.0 Balkan profile; higher organic fraction
msw_biogenic_frac.notes: Higher biogenic fraction consistent with regional profile.

msw_treatment.source: World Bank Serbia Situational Analysis 2023: 79.4% landfilled, 15.4% recycled, no WtE; some illegal dumping

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: FAO livestock Serbia; ~1.2M cattle, 3M pigs, 17M poultry; JRC Europe neighborhood data
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Significant pig and cattle sector. Wet manure ~40 Mt × 10% DM = 4 Mt odt.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: EEA proxy; Serbia ~7M population, WWTP coverage ~50%; EU accession process improving infrastructure
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: ~70 kt dry matter/yr. Low WWTP coverage limits sludge volumes.

nutrient_status_source: FAO fertilizer data; Serbia moderate fertilizer use; Vojvodina intensive but not at NL/DK excess levels
notes: Vojvodina province is a concentrated agricultural powerhouse (maize, wheat, sunflower, soy). Serbia has significant biomass energy plans under EU accession process. No WtE infrastructure. High landfill rate = large methane avoidance opportunity if waste managed. Danube corridor potential for CO2 transport.
